# Configure OAuth clients for AI agents and MCP servers

This page describes how to configure Consul Enterprise to register OAuth clients for AI agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. When an AI agent calls the next service, its sidecar uses the agent's client to exchange the caller's token for an on-behalf-of token bound to that service. To learn how delegation works, refer to [On-behalf-of delegation for AI agents](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/identity).

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Workflow

Complete the following steps:

1. Enable the `consul-ai` feature gate.
1. Configure the identity provider.
1. Register AI agents and MCP servers.
1. Define on-behalf-of token audiences.
1. Verify client registration.
1. Protect the registration records.

## Requirements

- Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric installed. Refer to [Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install).
- IBM Verify as the identity provider, with a client ID and secret that Consul can use to register service clients.
- AI agents and MCP servers in the `default` namespace and `default` partition.

## Enable the feature gate

The Helm chart enables the `consul-ai` [feature gate](/consul/docs/manage/feature-gates) when you set `ai.enabled` to `true`. Consul rejects a service registration that contains an `ai` block while the gate is disabled.

When you do not install with the Helm chart, enable the gate with the [`consul operator feature set`](/consul/commands/operator/feature#set) command:

```shell-session hideClipboard
$ consul operator feature set consul-ai enabled
Name       Stage         Desired  Effective  Eligible  Source    Reason            Min Version  Policy Index  Status Index
consul-ai  experimental  true     true       true      operator  operator-enabled  2.1.0        25            25
```

Confirm that the `Effective` column shows `true`. If it shows `false`, check the `Reason` column. Refer to [Feature gate states](/consul/docs/manage/feature-gates#feature-gate-states) for more information.

## Configure the identity provider

Complete the following steps before you register an `ai-agent` or `mcp-server`:

1. Create exactly one access control list (ACL) auth method with `Type` set to `oidc` and `EnableServiceDCR` set to `true`. The flagged method is the cluster identity provider. Consul waits to register clients when the cluster has no flagged method or more than one flagged method. Refer to [`EnableServiceDCR`](/consul/docs/secure/acl/auth-method/oidc#enableservicedcr).

1. Configure the following settings on the flagged auth method:

   - Set `OIDCDiscoveryURL`, `OIDCClientID`, and `OIDCClientSecret`. Consul uses `OIDCClientID` and `OIDCClientSecret` as the bootstrap client that registers service clients. `OIDCClientAssertion` cannot replace `OIDCClientSecret` for this bootstrap. Consul rejects the auth method for dynamic client registration when the secret is empty.
   - Set `JWTSupportedAlgs` to `["ES256"]`. IBM Verify signs tokens with ES256, and this field defaults to RS256.
   - Set a nonzero `MaxTokenTTL`. This field is outside `Config`, and Consul rejects an `oidc` method when it is unset. The [service registration example](/consul/docs/secure/acl/auth-method/oidc#example-configuration-for-service-client-registration) uses `1h`.
   - You can omit `AllowedRedirectURIs` when you use the method only for service registration.

Consul rejects an agent configuration block named `oauth.iam`. Configure the identity provider with the auth method instead.

## Register AI agents and MCP servers

Consul creates an OAuth client when you register a service with an AI role that receives one:

| Role | Sub-block | OAuth client | On-behalf-of credential |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ai-agent` | `agent` | Yes | Yes. The agent exchanges tokens for outgoing calls. |
| `mcp-server` | `mcp_server` | Yes | No. The server is an audience for callers. |
| `inference-model` | `inference_model` | No | No |

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="Kubernetes">

Set the `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role` pod annotation to `ai-agent` or `mcp-server`. Refer to [Register AI workloads](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install#register-ai-workloads).

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Service definition">

Register the service with an [`ai`](/consul/docs/reference/service#ai) block whose `role` is `ai-agent` or `mcp-server`, and set the one sub-block that matches `role`. You can set the block in a service definition file, the [catalog register API](/consul/api-docs/catalog#register-entity), or the [agent service register API](/consul/api-docs/agent/service#register-service).

An `inference-model` registration requires the same feature gate but does not create a client or a key-value record. Refer to the [`inference_model` block](/consul/docs/reference/service#inference_model).

</Tab>
</Tabs>

Consul registers one client for each service. It does not register a second client for the service's sidecar proxy.

## On-behalf-of token audiences

An on-behalf-of audience is the identity of the next service in the call. Consul builds the audiences for an agent from its explicit proxy upstreams in the `default` namespace, `default` partition, and local datacenter. For each upstream, Consul uses the destination service's registered client ID. You do not set an audience list on the service definition.

To let an agent exchange tokens for an MCP server or another agent, add that service as an explicit upstream of the agent. A service intention that allows a tool call does not add an audience.

Consul does not add an audience for a wildcard upstream, a centrally configured upstream, a prepared query, a peered service, a service in another datacenter, or a service outside the `default` namespace and partition.

To authorize tool calls from an agent to an MCP server, refer to [Define tool policy](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/tool-access/configure#define-tool-policy).

## Verify client registration

Consul stores each client's registration record in the key-value store at `oauth/<service>/state`, where `<service>` is the service name, not the service ID. The record's `state` field reports progress:

| `state` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PENDING` | Registration has started and is not finished. If the identity provider rejects the client, Consul retries and does not write a separate failure state. |
| `ACTIVE` | The identity provider accepted the client. Delivery of the on-behalf-of credential to an `ai-agent` can still be in progress. |
| `ROTATING` | Consul is rotating the client key. |
| `REVOKING` | The service was deregistered and Consul is removing the client. |

The record also contains the client's private key. When you check the state, extract only the `state` field so that the key does not appear in your terminal or logs:

```shell-session
$ consul kv get oauth/<service>/state | jq -r '.state'
```

<!-- TODO: Confirm the record's JSON field name for the state, and whether a way to check registration state exists that does not read the private key. -->

## Protect the registration records

<Warning>

The registration record at `oauth/<service>/state` is an ordinary key-value entry that includes the OAuth client credential and private key. Any caller that can read the key can retrieve it.

</Warning>

- When ACLs are disabled, every caller can read the record.
- A management token can read the record even when another policy denies the prefix.
- Do not grant `key:read` or `key:write` on `oauth/` to workload tokens. A token with `key:write` can replace the client ID and private key.
- A client agent loads this credential with a key-value read that carries no ACL token. Denying `key:read` on `oauth/` to the anonymous token can prevent that load.

## API

Use the following endpoints to configure the identity provider and register AI services:

- [Update a feature gate](/consul/api-docs/operator/feature#update-a-feature-gate) to enable the `consul-ai` feature gate.
- [Create an ACL auth method](/consul/api-docs/acl/auth-methods#create-an-auth-method) to create the `oidc` auth method with `EnableServiceDCR` set to `true`.
- [Register a catalog entity](/consul/api-docs/catalog#register-entity) to register a service with an `AI` object.
- [Register an agent service](/consul/api-docs/agent/service#register-service) to register a service with an `AI` object on the local agent.
